text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
24 CHASA

-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to urge on Monday state companies to cut higher than planned monthly wages in line with International Monetary Fund recommendations to curb budget deficit and spending. @
-- Bulgaria's Interior Ministry said it had stepped up security for Vassil Filipov, executive director of state gas monopolist Bulgargas after Filipov received anonymous phone threats to his life.
-- Bulgaria's grain traders said they expected the Agriculture ministry to curb grain exports by applying strict licensing regulations.
Bulgaria needs to import 53,000 tonnes of bread wheat to cover the gap until the new crop and a further 1.072 million tonnes of bread and feed wheat up to 1998. @
-- Bulgaria's monthly inflation in May is expected to be equal to zero, statistics experts said. Monthly inflation in April was -0.7 percent.
TRUD
-- Bulgaria's Prince Kiril, the son of exiled king Simeon II is expected to arrive in Sofia next week.
Kiril is an economic advisor of Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov.
STANDART @

-- Bulgarian police officers said they have cracked down on a channel to smuggle drugs from the United States to Bulgaria. The police said it had seized three kilogrammes of opium and 0.670 kilogrammes of hashish.

-- The parliamentary group of Bulgaria's People's Union, a part of the ruling anti-communist coalition said it would submit in parliament a bill to register existing political parties. Under the draft bill a political party should have at least 5,000 members to be registered.
Now in Bulgaria there are 206 political parties. @

-- Bulgaria's parliament budget commmission is expected to discuss on Tuesday amendments to the Bulgarian National Bank Act and the bill is expected to be approved by parliament by the end of the week, parliament officials said.
-- Bulgaria's state-owned Expressbank has posted some 1.37 billion lev profit for last year, private Balkan agency said.
-- Bulgaria has received a bid from a German company for its Varna shipyard, the yard's director Georgi Dichev said but declined to elaborate.
The Varna shipyard expects some $130 million income this year from the sale of seven ships. @
PARI
-- Bulgaria's state-owned Post Bank said some 180 million levs were siphoned from the its head office in Sofia through a documentary fraud on Friday. Bank officials declined any details on the case.
-- The average wage in Bulgaria in April was 123,000 levs ($78.34), National Statistics Institute figures showed. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
